 ATP Lyon Quarterfinal Predictions Including Taylor Fritz vs Daniel Altmaier 
 Share Share this article
 × X Facebook LinkedIn WhatsApp Reddit Email Copy 
 It should be an entertaining day of tennis at ATP Lyon with a number of the world’s best set to take to the courts and battle for a spot in Friday’s semifinals. As always, we here at LWOT will be offering our predictions for every match on the slate, as well as the action at ATP Brussels and ATP Almaty. But who will reach the last four?
 ATP Lyon Quarterfinal Predictions 
 Flavio Cobolli vs Brandon Nakashima 
 Head-to-head: Nakashima 1-0 Cobolli
 It is partly a testament to just how well he was playing earlier this season, but the last few months have been disappointing for Flavio Cobolli . One suspects that it might be a hangover from the manner of his loss in the quarterfinals at Wimbledon where he simply did not turn up. But there have been signs of life for the Italian recently and he has played some good tennis so far at ATP Lyon, not least in bringing the curtain down on Stan Wawrinka’s career.
 This will be a tough test for him though. Brandon Nakashima has also looked sharp so far this week and made short work of Kyrian Jacquet in the second round, beating the Frenchman 6-4 6-3. He is also probably better suited to the conditions in Lyon than the Italian, with Nakashima at his best when on the front foot and dictating. This has the makings of a close contest, but don’t be surprised to see the American pull off an upset.
 Prediction: Nakashima in 3 
 Luca Van Assche vs Lorenzo Musetti 
 Head-to-head: Van Assche 1-0 Musetti
 It has been a deeply frustrating year for Lorenzo Musetti, largely due to injuries rather than any particular loss of form. But he doubtless would have been hoping to play rather more than the 34 matches he has managed to play so far this season. The positive for the Italian is that it does look like he has found some form this week with comfortable wins over Matteo Arnaldi and Moise Kouame.
 Luca Van Assche, who has impressed himself in wins over his countryman Clement Tabur and third seed Valentin Vacherot, should pose Musetti a sterner test. But if Musetti plays his best tennis, or even anything close to it, he should have the beating of the Frenchman, even up against a partisan crowd at ATP Lyon.
 Prediction: Musetti in 3 
 Corentin Moutet vs Tommy Paul 
 Head-to-head: Paul 2-0 Moutet
 This instinctively seems like a difficult match-up for Corentin Moutet, and that is borne out by their head-to-head, with Tommy Paul having won both of their previous meetings, including earlier this year in Delray Beach. Moutet did win a set in that match, which should give him some hope, but he is not going to outlast Paul from the baseline and the American covers the court well enough that he should be able to track down enough of Moutet’s drop shots to take that tactic away from the Frenchman.
 Prediction: Paul in 2 
 Taylor Fritz vs Daniel Altmaier 
 Head-to-head: Altmaier 1-0 Fritz
 Somewhat surprisingly given the disparity in their rankings (and career numbers), Daniel Altmaier comes into this match leading the head-to-head having gotten the better of Taylor Fritz in four sets at the first round at Roland Garros last year. Will the German be able to pull off another victory at ATP Lyon? Stranger things have happened, but it doesn’t look particularly likely.
 Altmaier is not just a clay-court specialist, but that is unquestionably his preferred surface, whereas one suspects that Fritz would not entirely mind skipping the clay-court swing. At any rate, the American is certainly more comfortable on hard courts, particularly indoors where he gets most value for his booming serve and can keep the points short. If he plays to his strengths, he should have the beating of Altmaier.
 Prediction: Fritz in 2
